why: Multiple post-snapshot items surfaced: an arXiv preprint 'Certified Minimal-Prime Branch Closures for Odd Perfect Numbers' claiming to rule out odd perfect numbers with certain minimal-prime properties (a genuine case-restriction, if legitimate), plus several non-peer-reviewed claims (academia.edu, ResearchGate, SSRN, Zenodo) asserting full nonexistence proofs; none of these could be verified as credible or correctly dated, and the classic literature (Ochem-Rao bound 10^1500, nine distinct prime factors) predates the snapshot.
